+# Compiled Go lifecycle fixture contract
+
+**Status: frozen for E-FIXTURE (2026-10-31).** The fixture is an admitted-profile Go application with a finite, value-owned topology. It does not compile a generic manager or pointer graph.
+
+## Roles and state ownership
+
+Package `github.com/samuelpmahan/gondola/fixtures/compiled/lifecycle` exports the ordinary roles `Init() State`, `Update(State, gobi.Message) (State, []gobi.Effect)`, and `View(State) gobi.Node`. The AppIR component ID and package path are both `github.com/samuelpmahan/gondola/fixtures/compiled/lifecycle`; its state type is `github.com/samuelpmahan/gondola/fixtures/compiled/lifecycle.State`, and its message type is `github.com/samuelpmahan/gondola/gobi.Message`. `compiled-lifecycle` is the fixture's display name only.
+
+`State` owns four fixed value records: `Parent`, `Child`, `Grandchild`, `Sibling`, plus `NextRequestID`. Parent → Child → Grandchild form one root subtree. Sibling is a second root. Each `NodeState` contains `ID`, `ParentID`, `Generation`, `RequestID`, `Alive`, `Requested`, `Pending`, `Token`, `Reply`, and `Counter counter.State`. Parent, Child, Grandchild, and Sibling use the existing `counter.Update` for their Add messages. The screen is assembled with `gobi.Node` builders.
+
+The fixture deliberately models a finite set of four slots. `removeParent` marks the first root and its descendants dead; `remountParent` revives that subtree with higher generations and fresh counter values. It does not implement arbitrary child creation, generic identity maps, pointer receivers, shared mutable state, or a component Manager.
+
+## Messages and token rules
+
+The supported message names are:
+
+| Message | Arg | Go transition |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `addParent`, `addChild`, `addGrandchild`, `addSibling` | empty | Calls `counter.Update` with `Name:"add"` on that live slot. |
+| `requestParent`, `requestChild`, `requestGrandchild`, `requestSibling` | empty | Allocates a monotonic request ID, marks the live slot requested/pending, stores its token, emits one request effect. |
+| `removeParent` | empty | Emits pending cancellation effects in grandchild, child, parent order, then marks those three slots dead. |
+| `remountParent` | empty | Increments parent/child/grandchild generations, resets their request state and counters, and preserves the sibling. |
+| `complete` | exact token | Completes only a live pending slot whose stored token exactly matches. It stores the token in `Reply` and clears `Pending`. Unknown, canceled, stale-generation, and duplicate tokens leave state unchanged. |
+
+Tokens are constructed from the actual state values as `scope:g<Generation>:r<RequestID>` using `strconv.FormatUint`; the request ID is not derived from a hard-coded action order. The fixed script happens to allocate `parent:g1:r1`, `child:g1:r2`, `grandchild:g1:r3`, and `sibling:g1:r4`, followed after remount by `parent:g2:r5`, `child:g2:r6`, and `grandchild:g2:r7`. Requests stop before the JavaScript safe-integer boundary, and remount refuses to revive a subtree if any generation has reached that boundary, so generations and tokens do not saturate or repeat.
+
+## Effect ABI and lifecycle host seam
+
+Request effects use the admitted `fixture.request` effect and existing `gobi.Effect` value shape:
+
+```json
+{"Kind":"fixture.request","Name":"lookup","Arg":"child:g1:r2","Reply":"complete"}
+```
+
+Cancellation effects use the same four `gobi.Effect` fields:
+
+```json
+{"Kind":"lifecycle.cancel","Name":"cancel","Arg":"child:g1:r2","Reply":""}
+```
+
+The cancel `Arg` is the stable token from the originating request. A lifecycle host maps that token to its request correlation and cancels only that request. Cancellation is fire-and-forget. `removeParent` returns a dense effect slice in deterministic postorder: pending Grandchild, pending Child, pending Parent. The independent Sibling's request is neither canceled nor drained.
+
+The lifecycle runtime retains the existing strict request policy and opts into one narrowly scoped cancellation descriptor. The existing compiled runtime policy remains the default for all other consumers. A canceled host request must lose its runtime completion correlation; a late `runtime.complete` is rejected. The fixture also sends an explicit `complete` Go message with the old token after remount, proving the Go equality guard independently of the runtime correlation guard.
+
+Renderer replacement does not call `Update` or replace app state. Pending request tokens and callbacks remain owned by their lifecycle host until reply or explicit cancellation. The canonical script swaps DOM → React while all four initial requests are pending, then removes Parent.
+
+## Evidence boundary
+
+The native adapter replays the actual Go roles and Gobi view against [`fixtures/compiled/lifecycle/scenario.json`](../fixtures/compiled/lifecycle/scenario.json). The fixture's compiler gate uses the existing GoScript CLI. Browser/runtime evidence is recorded by the separate lifecycle harness and oracle lanes. This contract establishes only the finite fixture above; it makes no claim that arbitrary Go pointer managers or dynamic ownership graphs compile.

+# Compiled Go lifecycle
+
+This milestone compiles a finite Go-owned Parent → Child → Grandchild subtree beside an independent Sibling. The frozen fixture exercises effect requests, descendant-first cancellation, subtree removal and remount, stale and duplicate reply fencing, and a renderer swap while requests are pending. The Go fixture owns state transitions; the lifecycle host only tracks request correlations and delivers replies.
+
+The scope is the fixture in [FIXTURE.md](FIXTURE.md) and [CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md). It does not establish compilation for a general pointer-based Manager or arbitrary ownership graph.
+
+The AppIR `effect.request-reply` capability is a coarse effect-route marker. This experiment uses a closed lifecycle host policy for the exact `fixture.request` and `lifecycle.cancel` descriptors and retires canceled runtime correlations. The ordinary compiled runtime host still rejects `lifecycle.cancel`; another frontend must implement this explicit lifecycle profile and pass the replay before claiming cancellation support.
+
+## Run
+
+Use Go 1.24, Node 22, locked npm dependencies, and Playwright Chromium. The compiled frontend selects Go 1.27.3 through `GOTOOLCHAIN`.
+
+```sh
+npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
+npm ci --prefix interaction --no-audit --no-fund
+npm ci --prefix compiled-frontend --no-audit --no-fund
+interaction/node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium
+bash run-compiled-lifecycle.sh
+```
+
+The default full run first executes `run-compiled-methods.sh`, then runs Go suites and the browser, renderer, conformance, and shared-host runtime Node suites. It builds the native adapter and fresh React/DOM outputs through `go run ./cmd/gobi-build`, runs the compiled lifecycle runtime suite against the fresh React app directory, and then runs the native/direct/browser matrix and HTTP demo smoke.
+
+`bash run-compiled-lifecycle.sh --lifecycle-only` is an explicit partial route. It runs the lifecycle-specific chain but skips the inherited compiled-methods regression; the receipt and report label this mode.
+
+## Build and evidence layout
+
+Each invocation gets a unique directory under `compiled-lifecycle/builds/attempts/`. The React and DOM profiles each retain `request.json`, raw `result.json`, `buildmanifest.json`, generated `output/**`, and per-file output pins. The same attempt keeps command stdout/stderr, the native binary and trace, the demo site/screenshot, copied matrix traces, and a tar archive whose member hashes are checked after extraction.
+
+The browser harness writes a separate, fresh attempt under `compiled-lifecycle/conformance/evidence/`. The stable E-BUILD execution receipt and readable report live in `coordination/receipts/E-BUILD.json` and `coordination/reports/E-BUILD.md`. An in-progress receipt has `status: running`; only the final receipt reports acceptance.
+
+To view a successful local demo, serve that run's `demo/site` directory with a static HTTP server and open `/`. The demo exposes Go state, view, lifecycle effects, reply outcomes, renderer swaps, and runtime trace for inspection.
+
+## CI
+
+The `gobi-compiled-lifecycle` workflow installs the locked dependencies and browser, runs the same full entrypoint, and uploads the build archive and raw evidence even when a step fails.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Portable native-Rebalancer scheduling probe; all state/output paths are explicit."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import datetime as dt
+import json
+import pathlib
+import re
+import sys
+import time
+from typing import Any
+
+try:
+    from rebalancer import ProblemSolver
+except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - exercised by CLI users without dependency
+    raise SystemExit("Install the pinned dependency with: python -m pip install -r experiments/rebalancer/requirements.txt") from exc
+
+
+def now() -> str:
+    return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat()
+
+
+def read_json(path: pathlib.Path) -> Any:
+    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+def write_json(path: pathlib.Path, data: Any) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
+    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    tmp.replace(path)
+
+
+def review_id(extract_id: str, prefix: str) -> str:
+    suffix = extract_id[1:] if extract_id[:1].upper() == "E" else extract_id
+    return f"{prefix}{suffix}"
+
+
+def validate_token(value: Any, label: str) -> None:
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}", value) is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a safe filename token (letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen)")
+
+
+def make_state(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if spec.get("schema") != "chainspot.rebalancer-spec/v1":
+        raise ValueError("unsupported spec schema")
+    workers = spec.get("workers")
+    jobs = spec.get("jobs")
+    if not isinstance(workers, list) or not workers or len(set(workers)) != len(workers):
+        raise ValueError("spec workers must be a non-empty list of unique names")
+    for worker in workers:
+        validate_token(worker, "worker id")
+    if not isinstance(jobs, list) or not jobs:
+        raise ValueError("spec jobs must be a non-empty list")
+    prefix = spec.get("review_policy", {}).get("review_prefix", "R")
+    validate_token(prefix, "review prefix")
+    job_map: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    for entry in jobs:
+        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not entry.get("id") or entry.get("kind") != "extract":
+            raise ValueError("spec jobs must be extraction packets with an id")
+        jid = entry["id"]
+        validate_token(jid, "job id")
+        if jid in job_map:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate job id: {jid}")
+        allow_workers = entry.get("allow_workers")
+        if allow_workers is not None and (not isinstance(allow_workers, list) or any(w not in workers for w in allow_workers)):
+            raise ValueError(f"{jid}.allow_workers must contain only declared worker ids")
+        job_map[jid] = {**entry, "status": "pending", "worker": None, "started_at": None, "finished_at": None}
+    if spec.get("review_policy", {}).get("enabled", True):
+        for entry in jobs:
+            rid = review_id(entry["id"], prefix)
+            validate_token(rid, "review id")
+            if rid in job_map:
+                raise ValueError(f"review id collides with job: {rid}")
+            job_map[rid] = {"id": rid, "kind": "review", "depends_on": entry["id"], "status": "pending", "worker": None, "started_at": None, "finished_at": None}
+    policy = {"extract_priority": 100, "review_priority": 200, "repair_priority": 300, **spec.get("policy", {})}
+    return {
+        "schema": "chainspot.rebalancer-state/v1",
+        "service": spec.get("service", {}),
+        "workers": {name: {"job": None, "agent": None} for name in workers},
+        "jobs": job_map,
+        "events": [],
+        "epoch": 0,
+        "policy": policy,
+    }
+
+
+def load_state(path: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state = read_json(path)
+    if state.get("schema") != "chainspot.rebalancer-state/v1":
+        raise ValueError("unsupported state schema")
+    return state
+
+
+def init(spec_path: pathlib.Path, state_path: pathlib.Path, overwrite: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if state_path.exists() and not overwrite:
+        raise FileExistsError(f"state file already exists; use --force to replace it: {state_path}")
+    state = make_state(read_json(spec_path))
+    write_json(state_path, state)
+    return {"state": str(state_path.resolve()), "workers": len(state["workers"]), "packets": len(state["jobs"])}
+
+
+def exact_max_score(workers: list[str], ready: list[str], eligible: dict[str, list[str]], weights: dict[str, int]) -> int:
+    free = list(workers)
+    dp = {0: 0}
+    for job in ready:
+        nxt = dict(dp)
+        for mask, score in dp.items():
+            for n, worker in enumerate(free):
+                if not mask & (1 << n) and worker in eligible[job]:
+                    nm = mask | (1 << n)
+                    nxt[nm] = max(nxt.get(nm, -1), score + weights[job])
+        dp = nxt
+    return max(dp.values(), default=0)
+
+
+def solve(state_path: pathlib.Path, output_dir: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state = load_state(state_path)
+    workers = list(state["workers"])
+    jobs = state["jobs"]
+    lanes = list(jobs) + ["BENCH"]
+    caps = {job: 0 for job in jobs}
+    caps["BENCH"] = len(workers)
+    initial: dict[str, list[str]] = {lane: [] for lane in lanes}
+    pins: list[str] = []
+    ready: list[str] = []
+    eligible: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    weights: dict[str, int] = {}
+    for worker, record in state["workers"].items():
+        initial[record["job"] or "BENCH"].append(worker)
+        if record["job"]:
+            pins.append(worker)
+            caps[record["job"]] = 1
+    for jid, job in jobs.items():
+        if job["status"] != "pending":
+            continue
+        if job["kind"] == "review":
+            dependency = jobs[job["depends_on"]]
+            if dependency["status"] != "done":
+                continue
+        ready.append(jid)
+        weights[jid] = state["policy"]["repair_priority"] if job.get("repair_of") else state["policy"]["review_priority"] if job["kind"] == "review" else state["policy"]["extract_priority"]
+        eligible[jid] = [
+            w for w in workers
+            if not state["workers"][w]["job"]
+            and (job.get("allow_workers") is None or w in job["allow_workers"])
+            and (job["kind"] != "review" or jobs[job["depends_on"]]["worker"] != w)
+        ]
+        caps[jid] = 1
+
+    solver = ProblemSolver(service_name=state.get("service", {}).get("name", "rebalancer"), service_scope=f"epoch-{state['epoch']}")
+    solver.set_object_name("worker").set_container_name("packet").set_assignment(initial)
+    solver.add_scope("packets", {lane: lane for lane in lanes})
+    solver.add_object_dimension("headcount", {worker: 1 for worker in workers})
+    solver.add_scope_dimension("headcount", "packets", caps)
+    solver.add_constraint({"capacitySpec": {"name": "ready_packet_capacity", "scope": "packets", "dimension": "headcount"}})
+    solver.add_constraint({"avoidMovingSpec": {"name": "pin_in_flight", "objects": pins}})
+    forbidden = [{"object": w, "scopeItems": [job for job in ready if w not in eligible[job]]} for w in workers]
+    solver.add_constraint({"avoidAssignmentsSpec": {"name": "independent_review", "scope": "packets", "assignments": forbidden}})
+    affinities = [{"objectName": w, "scopeItemName": j, "affinity": weights[j]} for j in ready for w in eligible[j]]
+    if affinities:
+        solver.add_goal({"assignmentAffinitiesSpec": {"name": "ready_work_priority", "scope": "packets", "affinities": affinities}}, 1.0, 0)
+    solver.add_goal({"minimizeMovementSpec": {"name": "movement_tiebreak", "scope": "packets", "dimension": "headcount", "doNotNormalize": True}}, 1.0, 1)
+    solver.add_solver({"localSearchSolverSpec": {"solveTime": 1, "stopAfterMoves": 500, "randomSeed": 7, "moveTypeList": [{"singleMoveTypeSpec": {}}, {"swapMoveTypeSpec": {}}]}})
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    result = solver.solve()
+    elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
+    assignment = result["assignment"]
+    violations: list[str] = []
+    if set(assignment) != set(workers):
+        violations.append("assignment_worker_set_mismatch")
+    if any(destination not in lanes for destination in assignment.values()):
+        violations.append("assignment_unknown_destination")
+    counts = {lane: sum(dest == lane for dest in assignment.values()) for lane in lanes}
+    if any(counts[lane] > caps[lane] for lane in lanes):
+        violations.append("capacity_exceeded")
+    if any(assignment.get(worker) != state["workers"][worker]["job"] for worker in pins):
+        violations.append("pin_moved")
+    dispatch = {w: job for w, job in assignment.items() if w not in pins and job != "BENCH"}
+    if any(job not in ready or w not in eligible.get(job, []) for w, job in dispatch.items()):
+        violations.append("ineligible_assignment")
+    constraint = result.get("finalConstraint", {})
+    if constraint.get("brokenVal") != 0 or constraint.get("brokenCount") != 0:
+        violations.append("native_constraints_broken")
+    score = sum(weights[job] for job in dispatch.values())
+    optimum = exact_max_score([w for w in workers if w not in pins], ready, eligible, weights)
+    if score != optimum:
+        violations.append("nonoptimal_native_score")
+    if violations:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"native assignment rejected before dispatch: {violations}")
+
+    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    name = f"epoch-{state['epoch']:02}"
+    solver.save_bundle(str(output_dir / f"{name}.bundle"))
+    report = {
+        "epoch": state["epoch"], "at": now(), "ready_jobs": ready, "pinned_workers": pins,
+        "assignments": assignment, "dispatch": dispatch, "native_seconds": elapsed,
+        "native_constraints": constraint, "independent_capacity_check": True,
+        "independent_eligibility_check": True, "exact_score": optimum, "native_score": score,
+        "caps": caps, "eligible": eligible, "weights": weights,
+        "agent_by_worker": {w: record.get("agent") for w, record in state["workers"].items()},
+    }
+    write_json(output_dir / f"{name}.json", report)
+    state["events"].append({"type": "solve", **report})
+    state["epoch"] += 1
+    write_json(state_path, state)
+    return report
+
+
+def start(state_path: pathlib.Path, worker: str, job_id: str, agent: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state = load_state(state_path)
+    worker_data = state["workers"].get(worker)
+    job = state["jobs"].get(job_id)
+    if worker_data is None or job is None:
+        raise ValueError("unknown worker or job")
+    if worker_data["job"] or job["status"] != "pending":
+        raise ValueError("worker must be free and job must be pending")
+    latest = next((event for event in reversed(state["events"]) if event.get("type") == "solve"), None)
+    if latest is None or latest.get("dispatch", {}).get(worker) != job_id:
+        raise ValueError("dispatch must match the latest native assignment")
+    if job.get("allow_workers") is not None and worker not in job["allow_workers"]:
+        raise ValueError("worker is outside the packet's allow_workers eligibility")

+def validate_receipt(data: dict[str, Any], job: dict[str, Any], worker: str) -> None:
+    if data.get("job_id") != job["id"] or data.get("worker") != worker:
+        raise ValueError("receipt job_id/worker do not match the active packet")
+    if not isinstance(data.get("summary"), str) or not data["summary"].strip():
+        raise ValueError("receipt must include a non-empty summary")

+    state = load_state(state_path)
+    worker_data = state["workers"].get(worker)
+    if worker_data is None or not worker_data["job"]:
+        raise ValueError("worker has no active packet")
+    job_id = worker_data["job"]
+    job = state["jobs"][job_id]
+    path = receipts_dir / f"{job_id}.json"
+    if not path.is_file():
+        raise FileNotFoundError(f"receipt is not present: {path}")

+    job = state["jobs"].get(job_id)

+    p = commands.add_parser("solve", help="solve one dispatch epoch and write bundle/receipt")
+    p.add_argument("--state", required=True, type=pathlib.Path)
+    p.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True, type=pathlib.Path)
+    p = commands.add_parser("start", help="manually acknowledge one recommended assignment")
+    p.add_argument("--state", required=True, type=pathlib.Path)
+    p.add_argument("worker")

+    p = commands.add_parser("finish", help="release a worker after checking its receipt")

+    p.add_argument("job")

+    else:
